limitations: The PDF text layer corrupts Myanmar combining sequences. Preferred terms were hand-transcribed from rendered pages; extracted text was used only to navigate.
This is a terminology audit of the eleven listed confirmed terms across every string field in the four Myanmar-bearing files, not native-speaker certification or a complete retranslation.
The old textbook provides 1号 terminology only; 2号-only technical terms absent from the source remain unchanged and unresolved for textbook standardization.

Remaining synonyms and generic paraphrases were retained when they could not safely be tied to a confirmed technical term. No mass replacement of generic control, cleaning, contamination or safety wording.
Source page references are one-based PDF page indexes, not printed page numbers.
是正処置 in food-2-q148 is intentionally not normalized to 改善措置: canonical Japanese distinguishes them despite overlapping preexisting Myanmar wording.

sourceFindings: All eleven target technical phrases are supported by the rendered glossary. Singular/plural contextual suffix differences in CCP, management standards and corrective measures retain the same term stem.

Independently checked rendered glyphs for စီမံခန့်ခွဲမှုစံနှုန်း (管理基準), ပြင်ပအရာဝတ္ထု (異物), ကူးလူးညစ်ညမ်းမှု (交差汚染), and the longer hazard-analysis phrase against the actual page images. No corrupt text-layer sequence was introduced.

Japanese assessment fields reviewed for hazard analysis, corrective measures and cross contamination; all 管理基準 replacements correspond to canonical 管理基準. q191 retains separate Myanmar wording for 是正処置, and q148 remains excluded as intended.
Cross-contamination wording for human-mediated contamination in food-2-q095 is contextually supported by canonical 人を介する汚染 and rendered body page25.
limitations: This verifies the bounded eleven-term patch, not every original sentence or all source terminology.
No native-speaker/domain certification. 2号-only terms unavailable in the older 1号 reference remain outside the confirmed source inventory.
2024 terminology reference is not authority to change 2026 facts, numeric limits, procedures or requirements.
No repository file was edited during peer review.
